problems.latex: \begin{document} \section{Problem statement} In the following, a monoid is an integral, saturated, sharp, commutative, unital semigroup.  Monoids are written additively.  A monoid $M$ induces a translation invariant partial order on its associated group $M^{\rm gp}$ such that $x \geq 0$ if and only if $x \in M$.  A valuative monoid is a monoid in which the associated partial order is a total order. If $M$ is a monoid, $x \in M^{\rm gp}$, and $y \in M$, we write $x \prec y$ to mean that there are integers $m$ and $n$ such that $my \leq x \leq ny$. A monoid homomorphism $f : M \to N$ is called \emph{infinitesimal} if the following condition holds: \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$] \item If there are $x \in M^{\rm gp}$ and $y \in M$ such that $f(x) \in N$ and $x \prec y$ and $f(y) \prec f(x)$ then $x \in M$. \end{enumerate} If $P \xrightarrow f Q \xrightarrow g N$ are monoid homomorphisms, we say that $f$ is \emph{birhizomic} at $g$ if it is of finite presentation in the category of (integral, saturated, sharp) monoids and, for every factorization of $gf$ through monoid homomorphisms $P \xrightarrow h M \xrightarrow p N$ with $p$ infinitesimal, there is a unique monoid homomorphism $u : Q \to M$ with $pu = g$ and $uf = h$. A family of morphisms $P \rightarrow Q_i$ is called a birhizomic cover if, for every valuative monoid $V$ and every homomorphism $v : P \to V$, there is a factorization of $v$ through some $Q_i \to V$ such that $P \to Q_i$ is birhizomic at $Q_i \to V$. Let $P$ be a monoid.  Let $A_P$ be the category of monoid homomorphisms $P \to Q$.  The birhizomic covers form a Grothendieck topology on $A_P^{\rm op}$. Let $P$ be a monoid.  For any $x$ in $P$, there is an initial monoid homomorphism $P \to P[-x]^\sharp$ that sends $x$ to $0$.  Let $B_P$ be the full subcategory of $A_P$ consisting of homomorphisms $P \to P[-x]^\sharp$, for $x \in P$. We have given $A_P^{\rm op}$ the birhizomic topology and $B_P^{\rm op}$ the trivial topology in which all presheaves are sheaves.  The inclusion $B_P^{\rm op} \subset A_P^{\rm op}$ is left exact.  By left Kan extension and sheafification, it extends to a functor $\pi^{-1} : \operatorname{Sh}(B_P) \to \operatorname{Sh}(A_P)$ on the categories of sheaves.   Let $\pi_\ast$ be the right adjoint of $\pi^{-1}$. \paragraph{Question} \em Is it the case that, for all presheaves of abelian groups $F$ on $B_P^{\rm op}$, the morphism $$F \to \mathrm R \pi_\ast \pi^{-1} F$$ is a quasi-isomorphism? \end{document}

\section{Problem Statement} Let $D\subseteq \R^d$, $d\ge 2$, denote the $d$-dimensional Euclidean unit ball. Given a function $f\in C^\alpha(D)$ with H"older-Zygmund smoothness $\alpha > 1$ on $D$ and let $u=u_f$ denote the unique solution of the following divergence form PDE (Darcy's problem) \[ \text{div}(f\nabla u)=1~~\text{on}~D,~~~u|_{\partial D} = 0.\] Consider the non-linear statistical inverse problem of reconstructing $f$ from noisy measurements of $u$ corrupted by Gaussian white noise \[Y_n= u_f + \frac 1{\sqrt n}\mathbb W.\] For $r\in (0,1)$ consider the following class of conductivities \[ f\in \mathcal F(\alpha, r) = \{ h\in C^\alpha(D),~\|h-\mathbf 1\|_{C^\alpha(D)} \le r \},\]  where $\mathbf 1$ denotes a  constant function with value $1$. For small (but fixed) $r\in(0,1)$, what is the minimax rate as $n\to\infty$ for estimating $f$ in the ${L^2}$-mean squared error  \[ \inf_{\hat f_N}\sup_{f_0\in \mathcal F(\alpha, r)} \E_{f_0}\big[ \|\hat f_n-f_0\|_{L^2(D)}^2\big],  \] up to logarithmic factors?

Let $\Uc_q(\fb_+),$ $\Uc_q(\fb_-)$ be the upper and lower Borel subalgebras of the simply-connected quantum group $\Uc_q(\sl(n)).$ (This quantum group appears for example in the Klimyk–Schm"udgen book as $U_q^{ext}(\sl(n))$.) (1) Construct an explicit algebra isomorphism between $\bcS_n(\fB^*)$ and the generalized quantum double $\Uc_q(\fb_-)\,  \bipr\, \Uc_q(\fb_+)$ (with respect to the standard Drinfeld–Tanisaki skew pairing, $$\la \hat K_i, \hat K_j\ra =q^{\frac1n-\delta_{i,j}},\quad \la E_i,F_j\ra=\delta_{i,j}/(q^{-1}-q), \quad \la \hat K_i,F_j\ra=\la E_j,\hat K_i\ra=0,$$  in the notation of Klimyk–Schm"udgen). (2) Deduce that the algebra $\Uc_q(\sl(n))$ is isomorphic with $\bcS_n(\fB^*)/I$, where $I$ is the two sided ideal generated by $b_{ii}c_{ii}-1$ for $1\leq i\leq n,$ and $b_{ij}, c_{kl}$ are the horizontal arcs directed to the right: \BigonPGens \vspace*{.2in}

\begin{question} Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and $D\subset M$ a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. Does there exist an $\omega$-tame almost complex structure $J$ such that locally on $M$ there are smooth complex coordinates $(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ in which, for some $0\le r\le n$, the functions $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ are $J$-holomorphic and $D$ is given by \[ z_1\cdots z_r=0? \] Here one may first replace $\omega$ by a symplectic form connected to it through a path of symplectic forms, all cohomologous to $\omega$, along which $D$ remains a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. \end{question}

\begin{Ques}\label[Ques]{ques:main} Let $\mathbb{H}$ be a hyperfield with multivalued addition operator $\boxplus$. Let $x, y, z \in \mathbb{H}$ be elements. Suppose that $0 \in x \boxplus y \boxplus z$. Does it then follow that \[     0 \in x^3 \boxplus y^3 \boxplus z^3 \boxplus -xyz \boxplus -xyz \boxplus -xyz\text{?} \] end{Ques}
Does a 3-manifold obtained by Dehn surgery on an L-space knot have at most two prime summands?

Let $f:\S^2\to \S^2$ be a branched cover, $V(f)$ be the set of its critical values,  and $A, B\subset \S^2$ be  finite sets.  \begin{enumerate} \item If $f(A)\cup V(f)\subset B$, then every complex structure on $(\S^2, B)$ can be pulled back to a complex structure on $(\S^2, A)$, and this induces the map  $f^*:\Teich(B)\to \Teich(A)$.  \item If $A\subset B$, then forgetting the points $B\backslash A$ induces the map $i_*:\Teich(B)\to \Teich(A)$.   \end{enumerate} If $f(A)\cup V(f)\cup A\subset B,$ then the deformation space is defined by $$\D_f:=\{\tau\in \Teich(B): f^*(\tau)=i_*(\tau)\}.$$ Consider a quadratic rational map $f$ with critical points $c_1$ and $c_2$. Assume that  $c_1$ belongs to a cycle of length $4$, and the critical value $v=f(c_2)$ does not belong to the cycle. By taking  $$A=\{c_1, f(c_1), f^{\circ 2}(c_1), f^{\circ 3}(c_1)\}, \quad B=A\cup \{v\},$$ we get a deformation space $\D_f\subset \Teich(B)$. Its image in the moduli space is the set of conjugacy classes of quadratic rational maps with the properties described above.  Explicitly describe a simple closed curve $\gamma\subset (\S^2, B)$ such that a power of the Dehn twist around this curve preserves the deformation space, and its action on the set of connected components of $\D_f$ has an infinite orbit.

Let $M$ be a compact connected smooth manifold. Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. Assume that $X$ has the following property: If $f$ is a smooth function, and $u$ is a distribution, and we have $\mathcal{L}_X u = f$, then $u$ is a smooth function. Let $g_t$ denote the flow generated by $X$. Show that the flow $g_t$ has zero topological entropy.

Let $\M_g$ be the moduli space of genus $g$ Riemann surfaces.  We consider the Deligne-Mumford compactification $\overline\M_g = \M_g \sqcup \partial \M_g$.  The boundary $\partial \M_g$ admits a partition into strata  $\Delta_{G}$ parametrizing stable curves with dual graph $G$.   Let $V_0 \subset \M_g$ be a (complex) smooth subvariety of (complex) dimension $2$ that is totally geodesic with respect to the Teichm"uller metric.  Let $V_t$ be a holomorphic family of subvarieties of $\M_g$ deforming $V_0$, for $t$ in the unit disc $\Delta \subset \C$  \footnote{i.e. a complex submanifold $\mathcal V \subset \M_g \times \Delta$, with $V_t = \psi(\phi^{-1}(t))$, where $\phi: \mathcal V \to \Delta, \psi: \mathcal V \to \M_g$ are the natural projections; we will further assume that this gives a smoothly trivial family of submanifolds. }. We impose several technical assumptions on this family, namely (all closures below, e.g. $\overline V_t$, are taken in $\overline \M_g$): \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item \label{item:smooth} for every boundary stratum $\Delta_{G}$, we have that $\overline V_t \cap \Delta_{G}$ is a (smoothly trivial) family, and \item \label{item:compatible} the families so produced are compatible with $V_0$ in the sense that if the boundary of $V_0$ in a smaller stratum arises from its boundary in a larger stratum, then the same holds for $V_t$.  That is, if $\Delta_G, \Delta_{G'}$ are strata with $\Delta_{G'}$ on the boundary of $\Delta_G$, and $U$ is an open set in $\overline \M_g$ with  \begin{align*} \overline{\overline V_0 \cap \Delta_{G}} \cap \Delta_{G'} \cap U  = \overline V_0 \cap \Delta_{G'} \cap U , \end{align*} then, for all $t$,\begin{align*}  \overline{\overline V_t \cap \Delta_{G}} \cap \Delta_{G'} \cap U= \overline V_t \cap \Delta_{G'} \cap U. \end{align*} \end{enumerate} Note that we do \emph{not} assume that $V_t$ is totally geodesic for $t\ne 0$.   Now fix $\Gamma$ a dual graph; we will assume for ease of notation that $\Delta_\Gamma$ is a product of lower complexity moduli spaces $\M_{g_1,n_1} \times \cdots \times \M_{g_k,n_k}$ \footnote{for some boundary strata, we would need to quotient this by a finite group; we exclude those here}.  For each $i$, let $\pi_i: \Delta_\Gamma \to \M_{g_i,n_i}$ be the natural projection map. Denote by $\partial V_t$ the closure of $V_t$ in $\overline{\M} _g$ intersected with $\Delta_\Gamma$.  Suppose that $\dim \partial V_t=1$ and that each $\partial V_t$ is constant on some factor $\M_{g_i,n_i}$ of $\Delta_\Gamma$, i.e. for some $i$, $\pi_i(\partial V_t)=\{Y_t\}$ for all $t$.   Prove that the family $\partial V_t$ is non-varying on that factor, i.e. $\pi_i(\partial V_t) = \{Y_0\}$ for all $t$.

Let $H$ denote the hyperbolic plane lattice and let $E_8$ denote the negative definite $E_8$ root lattice. Let $\mathcal{X} \to \Delta$ be an $H$-polarised Tyurin degeneration of K3 surfaces, in the sense of \cite[Definition 3.20]{dfk3slpms}. Assume that this degeneration is very general, in the sense that the image of $0 \in \Delta$ under the map from $\Delta$ to the compactified moduli space of $H$-polarized K3 surfaces defined by Alexeev-Brunyate-Engel \cite{cmek3sspt} is not contained in any Noether-Lefschetz locus.  Let $Y$ be a very general $H \oplus E_8 \oplus E_8$-quasipolarised K3 surface. Then there exists an elliptic fibration $\pi \colon Y \to \mathbb{P}^1$ along with an allowable loop $\gamma \subset \mathbb{P}^1$ (in the sense of \cite[Definition 4.11]{dfk3slpms}), such that the $H \oplus E_8 \oplus E_8$-quasipolarisation is compatible with $\pi$ and $\gamma$ (in the sense of \cite[Definition 4.21]{dfk3slpms}) and such that $\mathcal{X} \to \Delta$ and $\pi \colon Y \to \mathbb{P}^1$ are a mirror pair in the sense of \cite[Definition 5.1]{dfk3slpms}. \providecommand{\bysame}{\leavevmode\hbox to3em{\hrulefill}\thinspace}\providecommand{\MR}{\relax\ifhmode\unskip\space\fi MR } \MRhref is called by the amsart/book/proc definition of \MR.\providecommand{\MRhref}[2]{ \href{http://www.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=#1}{#2}}\providecommand{\href}[2]{#2} \begin{thebibliography}{ABE22} \bibitem[ABE22]{cmek3sspt} V.~Alexeev, A.~Brunyate, and P.~Engel, \emph{Compactifications of moduli of elliptic {K3} surfaces: Stable pair and toroidal}, Geom. Topol. \textbf{26} (2022), no.~8, 3525--3588. \bibitem[GT24]{dfk3slpms} L.~Giovenzana and A.~Thompson, \emph{Degenerations and fibrations of {K3} surfaces: Lattice polarisations and mirror symmetry}, Preprint, May 2024, \texttt{arXiv:2405.12009}. \end{thebibliography}
